ads_analysis.account_level_diagnosis: Missed opportunity is primarily rank-constrained in non-brand search: the two in-scope non-brand campaigns show large lost-to-rank (51% each) while budgets are not being fully utilized (61–64% utilization), pointing to bid/ad-rank/coverage limits rather than daily budget caps. The biggest incremental volume sits in Non-Brand Search - Flights (356,440 missed impressions) and Non-Brand Search - Hotels & Packages (300,300 missed impressions), with Hotels additionally dragged down by weaker average quality score (5.1) and some wasted spend on low-intent service-policy queries.
notable_patterns: The two material campaigns both lose far more impression share to rank than budget: Flights lost rank 51% vs lost budget 16% with only 63.6% budget utilization; Hotels & Packages lost rank 51% vs lost budget 14% with 61.4% budget utilization.

Keyword evidence shows strong linkage between quality and coverage/performance: quality score vs impression share r=0.957 (p=0.0027) and quality score vs cost/conv r=-0.883 (p=0.0199). Hotels & Packages’ avg quality score is the lowest in the account at 5.1 while trying to scale.

Several high-quality, high-intent generics still have low impression share because they’re losing auctions on rank: e.g., “flights to spain” QS 8.5 at 34% IS with 66% lost to rank; “cheap flights europe” QS 7.5 at 30% IS with 70% lost to rank.

Query mix includes heavy competitor-brand zero-click exposure: 10,640 zero-click impressions, and 48.5% of search-term impressions are from zero-click competitor terms (e.g., “skyline journeys”, “coastal getaways”, “horizon holidays”), with only 0.5 conversions shown on a competitor term (“trailmark travel quote”).

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Large demand is being missed primarily due to rank: search impression share is 33% with 51% lost to rank vs 16% lost to budget, despite only 63.6% budget utilization. This campaign also contains at least one high-spend, low-intent/support query keyword (“flight booking customer service”) with QS 4.0 and £195.94 cost/conv.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Increase ad rank on proven high-intent flight generics that already show strong QS but low IS (e.g., “flights to spain” QS 8.5 with 66% lost rank) via targeted bid floors / tightening query matching, while adding/strengthening negatives for customer-service intent to stop paying for support traffic.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Scale is constrained by rank and quality: search impression share is 35% with 51% lost to rank (only 14% lost to budget; 61.4% budget utilization). Average quality score is weak at 5.1, and there is measurable waste on policy intent (“hotel cancellation policy”) with QS 4.5 and £116.36 cost/conv.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Prioritize quality-score uplift and tighter query controls for hotel/package ad groups (landing page/ad relevance), while excluding cancellation/policy intent; then selectively raise bids on best-performing, high-intent terms once QS improves to recover rank-related lost share.

recommendation_cards.title: Reallocate bids toward high-intent generics that are losing auctions on rank (not budget)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Both material non-brand campaigns are primarily rank-limited (Flights: 51% lost to rank vs 16% budget; Hotels: 51% rank vs 14% budget) while neither is close to budget-capped (63.6% and 61.4% utilization). At the keyword level, several strong-intent terms already have solid quality but very low coverage due to rank loss: “cheap flights europe” QS 7.5 has 30% IS with 70% lost rank; “weekend city breaks” QS 7.0 has 32% IS with 68% lost rank; “flights to spain” QS 8.5 has 34% IS with 66% lost rank; “all inclusive holidays” QS 8.0 has 36% IS with 64% lost rank.
recommended_steps: Create a short list of 10–20 ‘core’ non-brand generics (starting with the four above) and apply a controlled bid uplift / bid floor to win back rank where lost-to-rank is >60%.
Concentrate the uplift in the ad groups with the best QS first (QS ≥7) to buy incremental impression share efficiently; avoid blanket increases across the whole campaigns.
Review results after 3–5 days and keep only terms where incremental clicks hold efficiency (ROAS/cost per conv).
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Impression share on the four cited keywords moving from ~30–36% toward 45%+ while lost-to-rank drops by ~10+ pts (e.g., 70% -> <60%).

recommendation_cards.title: Fix Hotels & Packages quality score (avg QS 5.1) before trying to scale spend
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Non-Brand Search - Hotels & Packages has the lowest average quality score in the account at 5.1 and is missing scale with 51% impression share lost to rank (IS only 35%). Keyword-level evidence supports this as a root lever: quality score vs impression share r=0.957 and quality score vs cost/conv r=-0.883, suggesting QS improvements should directly help coverage and efficiency.
recommended_steps: Split Hotels & Packages into tighter themes (e.g., ‘all inclusive’, ‘city breaks’, ‘family packages’) and ensure ad copy/landing pages explicitly match the theme to lift ad relevance and landing page experience components of QS.
For the weakest QS clusters, replace generic RSAs with more specific headlines/descriptions aligned to the query classes driving spend.
After QS improves, re-test bid increases on the best themes to recover rank-driven lost share without paying purely via higher bids.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Hotels & Packages avg quality score improving from 5.1 toward 6.0+ and campaign impression share rising from 35% toward 40%+ without ROAS dropping below current 11.57.

recommendation_cards.title: Add negatives to stop paying for customer-service/policy intent dragging efficiency
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: There is identifiable spend on low-intent support/policy keywords with poor quality and high cost/conv: “flight booking customer service” QS 4.0 spent £372.28 at £195.94 cost/conv; “hotel cancellation policy” QS 4.5 spent £279.27 at £116.36 cost/conv. These patterns siphon budget from high-intent generics that are currently rank-limited.
recommended_steps: Add/expand intent negatives around support/service/policy (e.g., ‘customer service’, ‘contact number’, ‘complaints’, ‘cancellation policy’, ‘refund policy’) in the two non-brand campaigns, then re-check query coverage for unintended blocks.
Route genuine support intent to a separate, tightly capped campaign only if the business requires it; otherwise exclude it from acquisition campaigns.
Reinvest freed spend into the high-QS, high-rank-loss generics list (e.g., “flights to spain”, “all inclusive holidays”).
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Spend share on support/policy queries trending toward near-zero while overall non-brand cost/conv improves (using current outliers £195.94 and £116.36 as the ‘do not exceed’ benchmark).

recommendation_cards.title: Reduce competitor-brand ‘zero-click’ leakage to improve non-brand auction focus
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Search terms show 10,640 competitor-brand zero-click impressions, and 48.5% of search-term impressions come from zero-click competitor terms (e.g., “skyline journeys”, “coastal getaways”, “horizon holidays”), while competitor terms show negligible conversion volume (only 0.5 conversions for “trailmark travel quote” is surfaced). This can inflate impression volume without meaningful engagement, and distract optimization from core generics where rank loss is the main problem.
recommended_steps: Add competitor brand names as negatives in non-brand campaigns, except where there is proven incremental conversion volume that justifies a controlled conquesting test.
If conquesting is desired, isolate it into a separate campaign/ad group with dedicated ad copy and strict efficiency targets, instead of letting it blend into core non-brand.
Re-check search-term reports after negatives to confirm the 48.5% share of zero-click competitor impressions materially drops.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Pct of search-term impressions from zero-click competitor terms decreasing from 48.5% toward <20% while non-brand click volume and conversions hold or rise.

already_working: Brand Search - UK is highly efficient (ROAS 48.18 with 790.3 conversions on £9,631.08 spend) and is not budget-constrained (58.5% budget utilization).

Ad creation quality looks solid overall: 83.3% of ads are rated Excellent/Good (4 Excellent, 1 Good out of 6), so the biggest gains are more about rank/coverage and query control than rewriting everything.

Auction positioning is competitive at the top of page: self top-of-page rate is 66.3% vs competitors’ 53.9% on average, and self outranking share is 61.4%, indicating the account can win—especially if non-brand rank losses are addressed more surgically.

email_copy.banner_headline: GBP 316,559 tied up in rank-lost non-brand demand
email_copy.subject: GBP 316,559 in non-brand growth is blocked by Ad Rank (not budget)
email_copy.hook: Your non-brand campaigns aren’t actually being held back by the daily cap — they’re being held back by auction position. You’re running with a daily budget of GBP 6,200, yet still giving up a large share of eligible UK travel searches because you’re losing on rank before budget even comes into play.
why_now_bullets: UK travel benchmark impression share is 40.0%; your account is at 37.84% — and the gap is coming from rank, not spend.
You’re losing 47.0% of eligible impressions to rank while only 15.2% are lost to budget — meaning more budget won’t fix what’s currently blocking scale.
UK search competition is rising at 22.0% QoQ while you’re already rank-limited at 47.0% lost to rank — waiting just makes the same clicks harder to win.
email_copy.stat_sub: Rank-constrained non-brand coverage in the UK
email_copy.impact_line: Based on what your account is currently missing in non-brand auctions, there’s GBP 316,559 of incremental revenue opportunity this quarter — and it’s primarily locked behind Ad Rank and query mix, not a lack of budget.
email_copy.scope_intro: Below is where that missed upside is coming from, campaign by campaign, and what’s specifically causing the loss (rank vs budget vs query intent).
email_copy.cards_intro: The fix is straightforward: win back auctions on the handful of high-intent generics that matter, stop paying for support/policy intent, and tighten the hotel/package structure so quality improvements translate into cheaper coverage.
email_copy.working_intro: A quick reassurance before the changes: there’s already a strong foundation here — we’d be building on what’s working, not rebuilding the account.
email_copy.opportunity_intro: If we simply move coverage from 37.84% toward 40.0% while keeping today’s click rate as the baseline, the added volume below is the conservative, near-term payoff — with more upside once the quality and query controls lift performance.
email_copy.fix_title: Want me to map this into a 10-minute action plan?
email_copy.fix_body: Reply with “Tue” or “Thu” and I’ll send two specific time options — or just reply “plan” and I’ll write back with the exact first-week changes (no meeting needed).
email_copy.ps: P.S. This is one of those rare cases where scaling doesn’t require a bigger budget — it requires spending the same budget where you’re currently losing auctions on rank.
